::: {.lede}
Three open questions and two abstracts already published. The open questions
share a method: all of them are about how a brain weighs what it already
believes against what it is currently being told.
:::

## Open {.k-head}

::: {.entry}
::: {.meta}
Residency thesis &middot; BAP04-B-2026-6538 &middot; [in preparation]{.status .pending}
:::
### [Belief updating and sensory attenuation in schizophrenia](schizophrenia.qmd){.title}

Whether delusions track a failure of belief revision, a failure to attenuate
self-generated sensation, or both. A beads task and a force-matching task in
the same people.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.meta}
In design &middot; [protocol]{.status .pending}
:::
### [Akathisia as active inference](akathisia.qmd){.title}

Prediction error can be resolved by revising the model or by acting on the
world. Akathisia may be a pathology of the second route.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.meta}
In collection &middot; with the Department of Neurology
:::
### [Effort and reward in multiple sclerosis](effort-ms.qmd){.title}

Fatigue and depression overlap on every questionnaire that tries to separate
them. Effort-based decision making offers a behavioural separation.
:::
